title: TikTok 1: Where your $5 coffee money actually goes (Langfassung)

lines.text: You pay five dollars for a coffee.
Where does that money actually go? Let's follow every cent.
The beans, the milk and the cup usually cost well under a third of the price.
Roasting, shipping and the farmer's share are all packed into that small slice.
But a café doesn't just sell coffee. It sells a seat, a warm room and ten quiet minutes.
Rent for a busy corner is one of the biggest single costs.
Then the barista. Wages, taxes and training are often the biggest slice of all.
Add electricity, the machine, cleaning, and the card fee you paid just by tapping.
Whatever is left is the owner's profit, often only a few cents on the dollar.
Slow mornings make it worse, because rent and staff cost the same when the line is empty.
That's why the pastry sits next to the till. Extra items cover fixed costs far better than coffee.
So you're not really paying for the coffee. You're paying for the corner, the people and the time.
Next time you pay five dollars, which part do you think costs the most?
